newsitem.title: USA: Mo. governor's budget includes $230 mln tax cut.
newsitem.headline: Mo. governor's budget includes $230 mln tax cut.

text.p: Missouri Gov. Mel Carnahan proposed a $6.2 billion fiscal 1998 general revenue budget Wednesday that includes the elimination of a $230 million sales tax on food.

In his state of the state address to the legislature, Carnahan said elimination of the three percent state tax on food would be the "fastest and fairest way" to deal with a budget surplus that exceeds tax revenue limits under the Hancock Amendment to the state constitution.
Carnahan, who was sworn in for a second term as governor last week, also proposed a higher education tax credit of up to $1,500 a year.
The governor's proposed budget for the fiscal year that begins July 1 would increase the school foundation formula to $1.5 billion from $1.4 billion in the current fiscal year.
The budget also includes $264 million for the state's share of desegregations costs for schools in St. Louis and Kansas City.

A federal court hearing began this month on Missouri's bid to end its support for desegregating the Kansas City schools. The state has offered the school district a final payment of $314 million through 1999.

Proposed capital improvements total $343.5 million in the governor's budget. However, only about $20 million of that amount is expected to be financed through a prison certificates of participation sale, according to the state's budget office.
